summary: Iteration 10 validated the STRING-ID contract fix on the PHP backend (ephemeral PHP+SQLite harness at localhost:8888) plus frontend regression on the preview URL. 38 pytest cases -> 35 passed, 2 failed, 1 env-skip (92% pass). THE ORIGINAL USER BUG IS FIXED: every UPDATE/DELETE with a string id (c_qa_1, sp_qa_1, u_qa_1, r_qa_1) now returns 200 instead of 400 'id wajib'; POST accepts a client-supplied string id so localStorage and MySQL share the same key; string FK (customer_id='c1') on repair create works. HOWEVER two new real defects were found that still cause 'MySQL not changing' for the user: (1) repair field-edits are silently dropped by repairs/index.php PUT, (2) repairs/reply.php calls an undefined function -> hard 500.

critical.issue: FIELD EDITS SILENTLY DROPPED. store.js repairs.update() -> phpMirror.repair.upsert(items[idx]) sends the FULL repair object, which ALWAYS contains `status`. The PHP handler branches on `isset($b['status'])` and takes the status-only UPDATE path, so device_brand/device_model/serial_no/complaint/notes/technician_id/service_fee/deposit are NEVER written to MySQL. Reproduced: PUT {status:'pending', device_brand:'Samsung', complaint:'EDITED', service_fee:999000} -> 200 OK but GET still returns device_brand='iPhone', complaint='orig', service_fee=100000. This is exactly the user-reported 'query mysql tidak berubah' symptom for repair edits. FIX: branch on an explicit intent (e.g. only take the status path when the body contains ONLY status, or send {status} alone from phpMirror and always UPDATE all fields otherwise).

PHP Fatal error: Call to undefined function require_auth() at reply.php:13. includes/auth.php only defines auth_user() and require_role(). Every admin reply to a customer review returns HTTP 500 in production. FIX: replace require_auth() with require_role(['admin']) (which also makes the manual role check redundant).

minor.issue: Because the mirror re-sends status on every edit, `completed_at = NOW()` / `picked_up_at = NOW()` are re-stamped on each save, clobbering the original completion/pickup timestamps. Should only set them when the timestamp is currently NULL, or accept the client value.
Password change writes only to localStorage - no phpMirror.user.upsert() call. Password changes never reach MySQL, so the user cannot log in with the new password after a PHP-mode rebuild.
ENV-ONLY (skipped): uses MySQL-only DATE_FORMAT/DATE_SUB/CURDATE/YEAR/MONTH so it cannot run on the SQLite harness. Expected to work on the VPS MySQL, but NOT verified by this iteration.

No global exception handler. Uncaught PDOException/Error returns HTTP 500 with the raw PHP fatal error + file path + stack trace in the response body (verified on stats.php and reply.php). Information disclosure on a public VPS; wrap in try/catch + set display_errors=0.
MySQL-only syntax (FOR UPDATE, ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE). Verified working only via a test-harness SQL translation shim; correct for MySQL production.

integration_issues.issue: phpMirror.repair.upsert() sends the whole repair object including status, triggering the PHP status-only branch. Either the client must send a status-free payload for field edits, or the PHP handler must be fixed (see backend critical #1).

design_issues.screen: All page headers (Manajemen Pelanggan, Kelola User, etc.)
issues: Page title renders with an opaque solid-blue block behind the text (looks like a stray text-selection/highlight artifact rather than intended styling); likely a gradient bg-clip-text fallback not applying. Low priority, cosmetic.

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix PUT /api/repairs/index.php so full-object payloads (which always carry `status`) still persist device/complaint/fee/technician edits. Reproduce with tests/test_php_string_ids.py::TestRepairUpdateContract.
CRITICAL: reply.php:13 - require_auth() is undefined -> 500. Use require_role(['admin']).
Do not re-stamp completed_at/picked_up_at on every save.
Wire phpMirror into authApi.changePassword so password changes reach MySQL.
Add a global try/catch + display_errors=0 so PHP fatals do not leak stack traces to clients.
dashboard/stats.php was NOT verified (MySQL-only date functions) - test it manually on the VPS after deploy.
critical_code_review_comments: repairs/index.php PUT uses payload shape (presence of `status`) as the routing signal for two mutually-exclusive UPDATE statements. This is fragile and is the root cause of the dropped-edit bug. Route on an explicit action field or always UPDATE all provided columns.
PHP endpoints have no centralized error handling; every PDOException becomes a 500 with a full stack trace in the response body.

store.js keeps user passwords in plaintext in localStorage (users[idx].password) and mirrors them to the PHP API on every user update. Acceptable for a local demo, but it means plaintext credentials travel over the wire on every unrelated user edit.

config/database.php currently contains the TEST-ONLY SQLite bootstrap + a MySQL->SQLite SQL translation shim. This MUST be replaced by the MySQL PDO version (.bak) before VPS deploy, otherwise production writes go to /tmp/klinikkana_test.sqlite.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (login + 8 routes render, 0 console errors, phpMirror hook + _fire verified)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: rm -f /tmp/klinikkana_test.sqlite && cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_php_string_ids.py -p no:randomly -q. PHP server: php -S 0.0.0.0:8888 -t /app/php-backend (log /tmp/php-test.log). I added a TestPdo shim in /app/php-backend/config/database.php that rewrites MySQL-only SQL (FOR UPDATE, NOW(), YEAR/MONTH, ON DUPLICATE KEY) to SQLite so parts.php/settings/status-updates/rating.php are actually exercised; it does NOT cover DATE_FORMAT/DATE_SUB so stats.php still 500s (skipped). This shim and the whole SQLite bootstrap are TEST-ONLY and must be swapped for the MySQL .bak before deploy. Two tests are EXPECTED to fail until the developer fixes them: TestRepairUpdateContract::test_02 (dropped field edits) and TestPublicAndReview::test_04 (reply.php require_auth undefined). Frontend is still REACT_APP_DATA_MODE=local; window.__phpMirror._fire was confirmed to emit the correct PUT /api/customers/index.php?id=c1.
rca_of_the_issue: The original 'MySQL tidak berubah' bug had TWO layers. Layer 1 (fixed & verified this iteration): PHP endpoints cast ids with (int), so string localStorage ids became 0 and every UPDATE/DELETE returned 400 'id wajib'; all id columns are now VARCHAR(64), the (int) casts are removed, and POST accepts a client-supplied id so localStorage and MySQL share the same key - all 4 CRUD cycles (customers, spareparts, users, repairs incl. string FK) now pass. Layer 2 (still broken): repairs/index.php PUT decides between a status-only UPDATE and a field UPDATE based on whether the body contains `status`. Because phpMirror always mirrors the entire repair object (which always has a status), the field UPDATE branch is unreachable, so every repair edit returns 200 while MySQL keeps the old values. Additionally repairs/reply.php calls the non-existent require_auth(), producing a hard 500 on every admin review reply.
